# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 92 (Bu-Vb Pc92)

**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 92
**Title (English, from literature):** Making an oversize robe
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul0.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 92, titled *Sugatacīvara* ("Making an oversize robe"), is the final training rule in the Pācittiya chapter of the Theravāda *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga*. The rule provides that a monk who makes a robe exceeding the standard measurement of the Buddha's robe (*sugatānaṁ cīvara*) commits an expiation-requiring offense (*pācittiya*); the robe must be cut down to proper dimensions and the offense confessed. An English translation of the rule and its word analysis has been produced by Bhikkhu Brahmali. Secondary literature surveyed in the research dossier does not discuss the substance of this rule, generally citing "92 Pācittiya" only as the total tally of expiation rules in the Pātimokkha.

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on catalog and DharmaNexus data.*
